title: Continuity of a Function (Intuitive Definition)
notes: **Graphical idea.** A continuous graph has no break at the point: a tiny change in x produces only a tiny change in f(x), with no sudden leap or gap.
**Three conditions.** f is continuous at a exactly when (i) f(a) is defined, (ii) lim(x→a) f(x) exists, and (iii) the limit equals f(a); all three must hold.
**Common breaks.** A hole is removable, a step is a jump, and 1/(x − a) produces an infinite discontinuity at a; each violates a different one of the three conditions.
**Continuity on an interval.** f is continuous on [p, q] when it is continuous at every interior point, right-continuous at p and left-continuous at q.
**Worked example.** f(x) = x² is continuous at every real a because lim(x→a) x² = a² = f(a); polynomials are continuous on all of ℝ.
**Exam caution.** Drawing a smooth-looking curve is not a proof; state all three conditions explicitly when asked to justify continuity.
summary: Intuitively a function is continuous when its graph can be drawn without lifting the pen; formally that means no hole, jump or vertical asymptote at the point.
